title: STARTUP USA GUIDE
tagline: An independent, source-linked guide to federal and state funding for US startups.
disclaimer:
This site is an independent reference compiled to help founders find US federal and state programs relevant to startups. Unlike a single official government publication, it is compiled from many separate official sources — SBA.gov, SBIR.gov, Grants.gov, individual federal agency program pages, the IRS, USPTO, and each state's own economic-development portal.

Program details — funding amounts, eligibility criteria, deadlines, and application windows — change frequently and are not controlled by this site. Every entry links to its specific official source page and is re-checked against that source before publishing, but drift after that point is expected and not something this site can catch automatically.

This is a reference tool, not legal, tax, or financial advice, and not a government website. Before applying for, relying on, or structuring around any program described here — especially tax-driven ones like QSBS or Opportunity Zones — verify current details on the official government source linked from that program's page, and consult a qualified professional where the stakes warrant it.

This project began as an adaptation of startup-india-guide (github.com/fritzhand/startup-india-guide), which documents India's central government startup schemes from a single official playbook PDF. That single-source model doesn't exist for the US, so this edition uses a different, multi-source verification approach described above.
objective: This guide consolidates US federal startup programs — and a growing set of state-level incentives — into a single, searchable reference. It is designed to help founders find the right program for their stage, sector, and situation.
whoItIsFor: Immigrant founders navigating US visa pathways
howToUse: 1. Start with the Scheme Finder. Answer 5 quick questions to find programs suited to you. 2. Check the "What Do You Need?" Index for a need-based view (grant, loan, lab access, buyers, IP). 3. Use the Lifecycle Map to find programs matching your stage of growth. 4. Explore the full Directory for a structured overview of all programs with key details. 5. Deep dive into Program One-Pagers for full details including how to apply. Startup Focus Legend: Part A / Startup-Specific — startups are the primary or sole intended beneficiary; Part B / Startup-Relevant — broader eligibility (small businesses generally) but startups regularly benefit and apply.

structure: The guide opens with an overview of federal programs (17 documented in full), a Scheme Finder wizard, a need-based index, and a Lifecycle Map. Beyond the federal layer, it links to federal-agency innovation programs (AFWERX, DIU, NSIN, In-Q-Tel and more), a growing state-by-state schemes index, an incubator/resource-partner directory (SBA Small Business Development Centers, NSF I-Corps hubs, and accelerators) covering all 49 mapped states, and every state's official economic-development portal. A dedicated section covers startup-visa and immigration pathways for founders who are not US citizens or permanent residents — a topic outside the scope of the India edition this project was adapted from.
licensingNote: Most content here describes US federal government programs. Works created by the US federal government are generally in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. §105 (unlike the India edition's source playbook, which is a Crown/Government copyright work reproduced here with attribution). State-program and private-accelerator content is summarized from each organization's own public materials, with a link back to the original source on every page.
